newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: UNDCP, Pretoria seek to stem Africa drug traffic.
newsitem.headline: UNDCP, Pretoria seek to stem Africa drug traffic.

text.p: The United Nations Drug Control Programme (UNDCP) and South African police on Thursday launched an anti-narcotics project to stem drug trafficking from other African nations into the country.

Under the project, trained narcotics dogs will be sent to central and eastern Africa. Priority countries are Uganda, Tanzania, Kenya and Zambia. The project will be expanded into Botswana in December.

"These countries are strategically crucial in the fight against the narcotics trade, as they are situated on major drug transit routes to South Africa and internationally," police commissioner George Fivaz said in a statement.

Fifteen candidates from the first four countries' police services, excluding Botswana, are to undergo an intensive 103-day course as narcotics dog handlers at the police dog school in Pretoria, starting in January.
The amount of illicit drugs entering South Africa is increasing rapidly, both for local consumption and for trans-shipment to other points.
